meta.title: Combat Round Resolution
meta.subtitle: One melee swing end to end: swing budget, attack roll, best-of-all defense, three-channel damage

views.label: How many swings you get
views.note: calcSwingCount turns dexterity, weapon speed and skill into a number, then stamina and carried weight scale it down. Cap is 4 per weapon.

views.label: The attack roll
views.note: The attack score is dexterity plus combat skill, scaled by stamina, position and light. No mitigation value is read here at all.

views.label: Best-of-all defense
views.note: Every defense the defender can pay stamina for is rolled against the same attack roll. The widest winning margin is the one that counts.

views.label: Three-channel damage
views.note: Raw damage is one formula for all three channels. Mitigation is a percentage with a cap, and only then does variance get rolled.

views.label: Why you never see a number
views.note: The final integer is converted to a phrase before it reaches any player. GetDamageDescription is the only thing the room ever sees.

participants.label: Attacker
participants.sublabel: player or mob with a target

messages.label: engaged with a target
messages.note: Combat is driven by the world tick, not by a command. Every 4 second round, handleCombatRound runs once per engaged pair.

messages.label: how many swings for this weapon?
1 to 4, after stamina and carried weight
messages.note: calcSwingCount: dexterity, weapon speed and skill set the base, then a stamina multiplier and an over-capacity weight penalty of up to 50 percent scale it down. Hard cap of 4 per weapon.

messages.label: roll dexterity + combat skill
messages.note: calcAttackScore reads dexterity, combat skill, stamina, position, light and flight. It never reads armor mitigation. Armor only reduces damage that has already landed.

messages.label: one roll, shared by every defense
messages.note: The swing is rolled once. Each defense is then rolled against that single value, so the defenses compete with each other rather than with separate attacks.

messages.label: which defenses can you pay for?
dodge, parry, block
messages.note: Each defense has a stamina cost. A defense the defender cannot afford is skipped for this swing, so a tired defender quietly loses options.

messages.label: roll all of them, not just the first
messages.note: Dodge scales with dexterity and unarmed skill, parry with a weapon's parry rating, block with a shield's block rating. Those ratings are separate fields from mitigation.

messages.label: last-resort save, if the attack won
messages.note: MinDefenseChance, default 0.15, gives an outclassed defender a fixed chance to avoid a swing that already beat them. A matching MinAttackHitChance floor runs the other way.

messages.label: hit, miss, crit or fumble
messages.note: resolveDefenseOutcome orders the result: fumbles first, then crits, then the normal margin, then the two floors.

messages.label: stat x skill x weapon x channel scale
messages.note: CalcRawDamage is one formula for all three channels: physical uses strength, magical uses willpower, conviction uses charisma. A configured per-channel scale and a global multiplier finish it.

messages.label: subtract mitigation, capped
messages.note: ApplyMitigation reduces raw damage by the defender's summed equipment percentage for that channel, clamped to the channel cap (default 75 percent). A critical hit skips mitigation entirely.

messages.label: damage for this swing
messages.note: dice.RollStat derives its spread from the mean using the global RollSpread knob, so the shape of every roll in the engine moves with one number.

messages.label: turn the number into a phrase
messages.note: GetDamageDescription converts damage to a share of the target's maximum health and returns light wounds, serious wounds, critical injuries and so on.

messages.label: "causing serious wounds"
messages.note: The raw integer never leaves the engine. Attacker, defender and every spectator in the room read the same descriptive band.

cards.title: Swing budget
items: Dexterity, weapon speed and combat skill set the base swing count
Low stamina and carrying too much weight both scale it down
Hard cap of 4 swings per weapon, minimum of 1

cards.title: Landing the hit
items: The attack score is dexterity plus combat skill, with no mitigation term
One attack roll is contested by every defense the defender can afford
The defense that won by the widest margin is the one that gets narrated

cards.title: Damage and text
items: One raw formula serves physical, magical and conviction damage
Mitigation is a percentage with a per-channel cap, default 75 percent
The final number is converted to a phrase before any player sees it
